title: Floating Ferrofluid
description: Ferrofluid pooled on a little speaker, dancing to the music — the desktop ferrofluid-speaker gadget. The fluid gathers into one lumpy black mass on the centre of the cone and bristles into a cluster of Rosensweig spikes that pulse in real time: bass swells the body and throws the spikes taller and shoves the pool outward before it draws back, treble bristles it finer, and the cone breathes on the bass with a glowing dust cap. Turn on the mic to feed it live sound; with no mic it runs on a synthetic kick so it's never still. It's rendered per pixel from a metaball field in a WebGL shader — the surface normal from the field gradient, shaded like oily black chrome with diffuse, a tight specular, a procedural environment reflection and Fresnel sheen — over the coned driver, its dust cap and rubber surround. Move the mouse to lean the spikes like a magnet; lobes, pool size, gather, field/spikes, speaker drive, jitter, viscosity and hue are live.
